title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension
main_claim: Every jointly continuous Z_p-action on a connected n-manifold has nonzero kernel, which gives Hilbert–Smith in all dimensions. The method: assume a faithful action. A Witt group E_d(S^d) of sheaf categories generated by proper images of compact polyhedra (d odd, d>n) has a rational image in a fixed lattice L_d^{-1}Z u_d. The action supplies p^k integral 'character classes' z_i(a) whose rational images are equal and sum to 4u_d, so each is (4/p^k)u_d. That contradicts the lattice once p^k > 4L_d.

issues.location: Sections 2–3 (Thm 2.9 homotopy invariance, Lemma 3.1 cutoff, Thm 3.3 germ description, Thm 3.4 Witt localization)
issues.description: Not a demonstrated error, but a coverage caveat. The integrality contradiction depends entirely on the Witt-group formalism for categories generated by Rf_*R_B with arbitrary continuous f (not constructible). It needs homotopy invariance, the germ description of Verdier-quotient morphisms, and Balmer–Walter localization. If any of these failed, the z_i(a) could legitimately carry p-adic denominators. I spot-checked these steps and they look correct (cutoff neighbourhood N = X \ f(Δ\E), fullness and faithfulness of germs, the sign of the cylinder constant c being irrelevant, the dense-doubling identities ιd = dι = 2). I did not verify every sign and lemma in Sections 2.3–2.4 or Appendix A.
issues.evidence: Thm 6.8 uses: Prop 4.9 (ℓ_U is an integral isomorphism, via E_d(U) = 0 and split injectivity of E_{d-1}(U) → E_{d-1}(X)); Thm 4.7 (lattice, via Thm 4.3 induction with the Lemma 4.2 chases); Props 6.5–6.6 (covariance and homotopy, via Thm 2.9 on C_d). I checked each chain at the level of the stated lemmas and found no break.

coverage: The LaTeX section files are missing from build/ (main.tex \inputs sections/*), so I audited paper.pdf via pdftotext. Read in full: Sections 1, 3.1–3.4, 4, 5, 6, plus the statement and proof of Thm 2.9. Checked in detail: Prop 5.1 (Newman reduction, closedness of F_j, orientation via G = 2H); Lemma 5.3 (Haar averaging gives a degree-one invariant test); Lemma 5.4 (rational averaging retraction); Lemma 5.5 (nerve approximation, pU ≃ ρ pV, the odd-sphere telescope being K(Q,d)); Lemma 5.6 (a point whose stabilizer lies in p^kG gives m disjoint sheets); Lemma 5.7; Prop 5.8. Also checked Lemma 6.1 (character decomposition, compact direct sums), Lemma 6.2 (adjoints M_λ† = M_{λ^{-1}} and T† = T^{-1}, cross pairings vanish), and Prop 6.4. For Prop 6.4 I verified by hand S² = id, S† = S and S Q0 S = Q with diagonal entries 2e_i − id, giving Σz_i = 2[A]. Further: Prop 6.7 (T M_β = ζ^{-1} M_β T cyclically shifts D_i = ζ^i D_0), Props 6.5–6.6, Prop 4.9 exactness with both d mod 4 cases, Thm 3.6, the Lemma 4.2 chases, Prop 4.6 local signature, and the final count 4L_d/m ∈ (0,1). Sanity check: for a finite cyclic group action the degree of any invariant test is divisible by |G|, so the same machinery gives no contradiction there. That is consistent, and it places the p-adic input precisely in the averaging lemma. Spot-checked only: Sections 2.2–2.4 and the Appendix A signs.
